title: Saving the Last Pair: Alcon Survey Finds Contact Lens Wearers Save Lenses for Important Moments
summary: Alcon survey finds 72% of contact lens wearers have saved the last pair for a special occasion. See why checking supply and benefits before year-end matters.
body_markdown:
Media Release


Media release –


Tuesday, November 24, 2026


## Saving the Last Pair: Alcon Survey Finds Contact Lens Wearers Save Lenses for Important Moments


[PDF](https://alcon.widen.net/s/rmxk62j2vv/saving-the-last-pair-alcon-survey-finds-contact-lens-wearers-save-lenses-for-important-moments_mediaalert)Print


- **Nearly three in four contact lens wearers have saved their last available pair or a fresh pair for an important day or occasion, including travel, job interviews, dates, holiday photos and weddings***
- **Two in three contact lens wearers have reached their final available pair without another supply ready1**
- **Only 41% of U.S. adults enrolled in vision benefits were aware before the survey that HSA or FSA funds could be used to help save money when purchasing vision-related items***


November 24, 2026


From holiday photos and vacations to dates and job interviews, contact lens wearers are saving fresh or final pairs for the moments that matter most. New Alcon survey findings show nearly three in four have done so, while two in three have reached their final available pair without another supply ready.1 With year-end approaching, the findings point to a practical step consumers can take now: check their supply and review available vision insurance benefits and eligible health savings accounts (HSAs) or flexible spending accounts (FSAs) funds before holiday plans arrive.


For the 72% of contact lens wearers who have saved contacts for a special day or occasion,* replenishment becomes more than just a supply check. It’s a reason to consider how vision insurance benefits or available HSA or FSA funds could help keep contacts on hand for everyday plans, not just special occasions.


**A Year-End Opportunity to Be Ready for the Moments That Matter**


Reviewing vision insurance benefits and available HSA or FSA funds may help consumers move from saving a pair for one important day to planning a more complete supply. Nearly four in five surveyed U.S. adults enrolled in vision benefits say a reminder about unused HSA or FSA funds could motivate a larger or more complete vision care purchase.* Yet only 41% were aware before the survey that HSA or FSA funds could be used to help save money when purchasing vision-related items.*


“Patients may be enrolled in benefits without fully understanding how or when to use them,” said Optometrist, Dr. Aaron Luekenga of Heritage Valley Eye Center in Santa Paula, CA.** “Learning more about insurance plan details and consulting with an Eye Care Professional before year-end can help patients avoid a supply gap and make informed choices about their vision correction and contact lenses.”


Vision insurance coverage and benefit reset dates vary by plan. FSA and HSAs are separate from vision insurance. FSA funds generally must be used by the plan’s deadline, although an employer’s plan may allow a limited carryover or a grace period. HSA funds generally remain in the account until used and do not expire at year-end. Consumers should confirm coverage, eligible expenses and applicable deadlines with their plan administrator.


**Why Wearers End Up Saving the Last Pair**


Cost, benefit timing and supply awareness can all contribute to the squeeze revealed in the survey. Forty percent of contact lens wearers cite cost as a reason for delaying replenishment, 31% have delayed purchasing a new supply while waiting for vision benefits to reset or become available, and 28% did not realize they were running low until they were almost out.*


“No one wants to realize the pair they were saving for a holiday gathering, trip or important photo is also their last,” said Dr. Carla Mack, Head, Global and U.S. Professional Education and Development, Vision Care. “These findings are a timely reminder to plan ahead, understand the benefits available to you and talk with your Eye Care Professional about your distinct vision care needs.”


As the year draws to a close, consumers can take a few simple steps: check their contact lens supply, review their vision insurance and any available FSA or HSA funds, confirm coverage and deadlines with their plan administrator, and talk with their Eye Care Professional about their vision needs and appropriate contact lens options.


The End-of-Year Benefits Consumer Insights Research was conducted among 1,000 nationally representative U.S. adults ages 18 and older enrolled in vision benefits. Findings specific to contact lens wearers are based on 324 respondents.


For information about using FSA or HSA funds for contact lenses, consumers can visit the[MyAlcon consumer benefits page](https://www.myalcon.com/contact-lenses/hsa-fsa-benefits/) . Eye Care Professionals can visit the[MyAlcon professional benefits page](https://www.myalcon.com/professional/contact-lenses/hsa-fsa-benefits/) .


Wakefield Research, September 2026, Results of any sample are subject to sampling variation.
